title: How Do You Run a Decision Log?
seoTitle: How to Run a Decision Log (With a Simple Template) | Chase Arenella
description: A decision log records what you decided, why, and what would prove you wrong. A simple template and the habits that make one actually work.
answer: Write down each meaningful decision when you make it: what you chose, the options you rejected, why, and what result would tell you it was wrong. Then set a date to review it. The review is what turns a log into a learning system.

sections.heading: Why keep a decision log
paragraphs: Memory rewrites history. A month after a decision, people remember the reasoning that matches the outcome, not the reasoning they actually used. A log captures the thinking before the result is known, so you can judge the decision on its merits instead of its luck.
It also solves a quieter problem: new team members can see why things are the way they are, instead of reopening settled questions.

sections.heading: A simple template
paragraphs: Keep each entry short enough to write in five minutes. If it takes longer, nobody will keep it up.

items: Date and owner: who made the call and when.
Options considered: the two or three real alternatives.
Reasoning: the main reason, plus what you knew and didn't know.
Kill criteria: the result that would make you reverse it.

sections.heading: Which decisions to log
paragraphs: Not every choice. Log decisions that are expensive to reverse, that affect more than one team, or that people will ask about later. A good rule: if you'd have to explain it in a meeting six months from now, log it today.
Skip routine calls. A log full of trivia gets ignored, and then the important entries get ignored with it.

sections.heading: Making the review stick
paragraphs: Put the review date on a calendar the moment you write the entry. When it arrives, answer three questions: what happened, did the kill criteria trigger, and what would we do differently with the same information?
That last question matters. It separates a bad decision from a good decision with a bad outcome, which is the whole point of keeping the log.

faqs.q: What tool should a decision log live in?
faqs.a: Wherever the team already works: a shared doc, a wiki page, or a single spreadsheet. The best tool is the one people will open without being reminded.

faqs.q: Can AI help maintain a decision log?
faqs.a: Yes, for drafting entries from meeting notes and reminding owners about review dates. The reasoning and the kill criteria should still come from the person accountable for the call.
